clue.text: Special clothes pleased some newspapers

parts.note: pleased means glad
rags is a slangy, dismissive word for newspapers, especially tabloids

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to have their smart outfit featured in several papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's best clothes, worn for a special occasion.

clue.text: Fired up in fight for knife

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed piece sits inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or argument

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: fired, as of a fire or fuse, means lit

explanation.surface: A weapon is drawn when a brawl heats up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'up' reads the word backwards; 'in' sets it inside SET-TO, a British word for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender, tapering blade, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Stronghold I'm in is very very noisy

parts.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold

indicators.note: in places the contraction of I am inside the pair of words that follow

parts.note: very can be replaced by so, as in so good
I'm written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone holed up in a fortress complains that it is extremely loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'very' does two jobs: the first is wordplay, the second starts the definition. 'in' puts the I'm piece between the S of 'is' and 'so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortissimo is the musical direction meaning play extremely loudly, one step beyond forte.

clue.text: Promote nurse

definitions.meaning: to promote or encourage the growth of something
to nurse or bring up a child not one's own

explanation.surface: A hospital worker gets moved up a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Foster is both a verb for encouraging development and one for raising someone else's child, which nurse covers.

clue.text: Man holding spades is hopeful

indicators.note: holding means the man's name wraps around the card-suit letter

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A gardener gripping his shovels feels optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'hopeful' is an adjective; 'is' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosy outlook is a promising, optimistic one, so rosy describes hopeful prospects.

clue.text: Manned it at sea, together

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crew staffed the vessel while out on the ocean, working as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the eight letters of MANNED IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in tandem means doing something jointly, side by side, so the phrase means together.

clue.text: Special mark obtained by Greek character? About time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the Greek letter wraps around the time abbreviation

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A distinctive symbol on a Greek letter prompts an impatient 'about time!'
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'Greek character' is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, or literally a distinguishing mark such as a brand or the stigmata.

clue.text: Austrian composer and US author heading firstly for island

indicators.note: one letter goes in for, replacing, the other

parts.note: Norman Mailer was an American novelist

indicators.note: firstly picks the opening letter of the word heading

explanation.surface: A link is drawn between a Viennese musician and an American writer bound for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of MAILER is swapped for H, the first letter of 'heading'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was the Austro-Bohemian composer of ten symphonies and Das Lied von der Erde.

clue.text: Wasted opening in ball game

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: An opportunity is squandered at the start of a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' looks like 'thrown away', but here it is slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, the same sense as wasted.

clue.text: Model drunk? Take no action

parts.note: to sit, as for a portrait, is to model
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: An inebriated fashion model is advised to do nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is an idiom for staying put and waiting rather than doing anything.

clue.text: Excessive devotion adroitly put in a new light

indicators.note: putting something in a new light presents it differently, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fanatical worship is cleverly reframed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is literally worship of idols, and by extension extreme admiration of a person or thing.

clue.text: Figure that's less sensitive

definitions.meaning: more numb, the comparative of numb, meaning less able to feel

explanation.surface: A statistic is called the less emotionally touchy one.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as NUMB-ER, rhyming with plumber, not the counting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a digit or numeral, while numbness is a loss of feeling, so more numb is less sensitive.

clue.text: Planner, furious about wrong name put inside

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for furious goes round the rest

parts.note: mad means furious, angry

indicators.note: put inside means the word for name is placed within the word for wrong

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: An organiser is enraged at a mistaken name on a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' looks like an anagram signal but is a noun meaning sin; 'put inside' and 'about' are two nested containers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastermind is the person who plans and directs a complex scheme, a chief planner.

clue.text: Intimate meal date overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the date letter is dropped

parts.note: dinner is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A cosy romantic dinner where someone forgot the date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' is the adjective, as in one's inner thoughts, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private and personal ones, the same sense as intimate thoughts.

clue.text: Quiet trip before marriage causes loud quarrel

parts.note: sh is the instruction to be quiet
an outing is a trip
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A peaceful jaunt before a wedding ends in a raging row.
explanation.definitionFit: A shouting match is an idiom for a heated argument in which people yell at each other.

clue.text: Embroidered cloth — videos sample

parts.note: video recordings were once on tapes
to sample is to try

explanation.surface: Videos give an example of a decorated textile.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven or needlework wall hanging, a decorated fabric.

clue.text: Send maiden over in carriage

indicators.note: in places the cricket abbreviation within the word for carriage

parts.note: transit is the carrying of goods or people
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over, one with no runs

explanation.surface: A young woman is dispatched across in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is six balls, and a maiden over is one where no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to send something on, such as a signal or message.

clue.text: Revered husband acknowledged

parts.note: allowed means admitted or acknowledged, as in allowed that he was right

explanation.surface: A spouse is publicly honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or deeply respected, as in hallowed ground.

clue.text: One looking after another round Aintree's far end in gallop

indicators.note: round means the carer's word surrounds the picked letter

parts.note: a carer looks after another person

indicators.note: the far end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A minder accompanies someone round the far side of Aintree racecourse at full tilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong at speed, as a galloping horse does.

clue.text: Cub reporter from broadsheet in Tinseltown

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A junior journalist on a serious paper is posted to Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt across 'broadsheeT IN TINseltown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintin is Hergé's comic-strip boy journalist, a young reporter.

clue.text: In my opinion, after gym, boy must go into assembly

indicators.note: after says the remaining pieces follow the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: go into means the word for boy is placed inside the word for assembly

parts.note: a rally is a mass assembly
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone opines that after a workout, a lad should attend a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Personally, used as a sentence adverb, means speaking for oneself, giving a private view.

clue.text: Accelerate round marker ahead

parts.note: O is a round shape
a pen is a marker, as in marker pen
up means ahead, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: Drive faster round the cone in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up a vehicle is to increase speed by opening the throttle.

clue.text: Spite shown by male meeting Christopher Robin's nurse

parts.note: in A. A. Milne's poem Buckingham Palace, Christopher Robin goes down with Alice, his nanny

explanation.surface: A man meets a nanny from a children's poem and behaves spitefully.
explanation.walkthrough: A. A. Milne's verse runs 'They're changing guard at Buckingham Palace, Christopher Robin went down with Alice.'
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm or upset others, which is spite.

clue.text: Reported diarist who ordered erotic entertainment

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is given by how it is said

parts.note: Samuel Pepys was the famous 17th-century English diarist, said as peeps

indicators.note: ordered means put into a different order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seventeenth-century diarist is said to have commissioned some racy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' says PEPYS aloud as PEEPS; 'ordered' turns WHO into HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep show is a sequence of pictures or a live performance viewed through a small hole, often sexual.

clue.text: Spy briefly in plot

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a plant is a spy or agent placed inside an organisation

explanation.surface: An agent is involved in a short conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot can be a scheme or design for doing something, which a plan also is.

clue.text: Count, after support, is on the wagon

indicators.note: after says the count word comes behind the support word

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
to total is to count up, or a total is a count

explanation.surface: An aristocrat, after propping himself up, has quit drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' suggests a nobleman, but it is the sum.
explanation.definitionFit: On the wagon is an idiom for abstaining from alcohol, which is what teetotal describes.

clue.text: Educational institution — it's for both men and women

parts.note: uni is short for university
it is a euphemism for sex, as in doing it

explanation.surface: A university says it caters to everyone regardless of gender.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex describes clothes, toilets or styles designed to suit either gender.

clue.text: Drink on break, and a biscuit

indicators.note: on puts the drink word in front of, upon, the break word

parts.note: brandy is a spirit drink
to snap is to break

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink during their tea break, with a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp, rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream.
